rubrics.criterion: The Date/Error/RegExp traversal decisions of each deep rewriting utility (DeepPartial, DeepWritable, DeepReadonly, DeepNullable, DeepUndefinable, DeepNonNullable, DeepRequired, DeepPick, DeepOmit, and their internal traversal aliases) are carried as one bundled, named unit — a single policy value declared once per boundary — instead of loose per-family boolean type parameters declared and forwarded individually; whatever shape the solver chooses (options record, policy type, or equivalent), no deep-rewriting type alias in lib/ keeps separately declared per-family boolean members for this group.
rubrics.rationale: This case's injected state decomposes one cohesive built-in traversal policy into three standalone switches repeated at every recursion boundary of nine modules; the core outcome is that the group travels and evolves as a unit again. Any sound bundling — the upstream record style or another equally single-value representation — satisfies this.

rubrics.criterion: Each utility keeps computing exactly the built-in-leaf results it computes in the current state: DeepPartial, DeepWritable, DeepRequired and DeepReadonly keep descending into Error (rewriting Error fields deeply) while keeping Date and RegExp as leaves; DeepNullable, DeepUndefinable, DeepNonNullable, DeepPick and DeepOmit keep treating all three families as leaves; the per-utility default configuration representing these outcomes is expressed in the new bundled form rather than as recomputed loose literals in each file.
rubrics.rationale: The rollout was supposed to be behavior-preserving configurability; four distinct default configurations exist across the nine modules and the refactor must reproduce all four without flipping any family's traversal outcome.

rubrics.criterion: The mapping from the bundled policy to a utility's traversal leaf set exists as one shared mechanism for the deep family — the per-file switch-combining machines (one private helper alias per module, each with its own flag orientation) are replaced by a single derivation the whole family uses, so adding a built-in family or documenting the policy no longer requires per-module edits.
rubrics.rationale: Beyond moving the values, the case injected nine divergent local encodings of the same leaf-set computation (different names, different true/false meanings, one utility with an extra Error branch, one with unconstrained literal defaults); consolidating the derivation is the difference between a cosmetic patch and a real resolution.

rubrics.criterion: DeepReadonly's user-facing override-record configuration keeps working with identical results: partial object-style overrides (for example overriding only the date family) still merge over the default configuration and change only the overridden families' traversal, without existing callers having to pass new arguments or switch to a different configuration style.
rubrics.rationale: The public record contract for DeepReadonly predates this case's injected rollback and is load-bearing for real users; a bundled design that drops or re-spells the override surface breaks the compatibility boundary stated in the task prompt.

rubrics.criterion: Consumers of the deep family keep compiling and computing unchanged types with no new explicit arguments: composite utilities that build on the deep rewriters (for example the Buildable = DeepPartial<DeepWritable<Type>> composition) and the strict deep-pick/deep-omit wrappers continue to work purely on defaults, and their source files need no changes beyond what the consolidation requires to compile.
rubrics.rationale: The injected rollout deliberately stopped at the nine utilities and left consumers untouched; the repair must keep that boundary intact — pushing new arguments into consumers would signal an API break, not a cleanup.

rubrics.criterion: The abandoned rollout machinery is fully removed or absorbed: the nine per-module combining aliases (DeepPartialBuiltin, WritableBuiltin, NullableBuiltin, UndefinableBuiltin, NonNullableBuiltin, RequiredBuiltin, ConditionalBuiltin, PickBuiltin, OmitBuiltin) and their explanatory comments no longer exist as divergent per-file copies — any leaf-set helper that remains is shared by the family rather than re-implemented per module.
rubrics.rationale: These aliases exist only to recombine the loose switches; leaving several module-local variants behind means the duplication itself survived the refactor even if the flag names changed.

rubrics.criterion: Vestigial policy plumbing survives the refactor: some deep utility still declares (or keeps forwarding) per-family boolean or policy members that no longer influence its computed traversal, a private per-family helper alias remains but is no longer referenced, or a dead default-policy union is re-declared in more than one module after the consolidation.
rubrics.rationale: A partial edit that renames the group into one module while leaving threaded-but-unread members or orphaned helpers elsewhere would look consolidated while preserving the injected clutter and its review cost.

rubrics.criterion: Built-in traversal outcomes are silently changed or blurred: e.g. one of the Error-rewriting utilities (DeepPartial, DeepWritable, DeepRequired, DeepReadonly) starts treating Error as an untouched leaf or returns a different type for Error-bearing shapes; a nullability or filter utility starts descending into Date, Error or RegExp; or merged DeepReadonly overrides no longer reproduce today's merged results.
rubrics.rationale: The whole injected rollout is default-preserving, so any per-family outcome flip in the repair is a behavioral regression introduced by the refactor itself and invisible to casual review of flag names.

rubrics.criterion: The type-level assertion suite is weakened to accommodate the refactor instead of the types being made correct: existing Assert/IsExact cases in lib/**/*.test.ts are deleted, skipped, gated behind a version condition, or relaxed (for example from exact-type equality to one-way assignability), or test helper definitions in test-types.ts are trimmed to make failing cases disappear.
rubrics.rationale: In this repository the 1,117 type-level assertions are the complete behavioral specification; silently shrinking them turns a failed refactor into a green one and destroys the test evidence future maintainers rely on.

rubrics.criterion: The repair expands into unrelated option domains or unrelated modules: settings owned by the path utilities (recursion depth, array-index accessors in lib/paths) are re-modeled to use the new policy abstraction, or unrelated utility families (mark/merge/dictionary/opaque or runtime function helpers) receive drive-by restructuring not required by the built-in policy consolidation.
rubrics.rationale: The task prompt states that path-utility settings are a separate options domain; bundling unrelated settings or gratuitously reshaping untouched families would smuggle new risk into what should be a scoped cleanup.
